theorem.input: Graph C with exact lists L(v) subseteq [4] and a vertex separator S of size 3.
theorem.separator_assignments: Col_L(S) is the set of assignments psi:S->[4] that respect exact lists and are proper on C[S].
theorem.components: Let Q_1,...,Q_t be the connected components of C-S.
theorem.boundary_lists: For psi in Col_L(S), define L_i^psi(x)=L(x) minus colors psi(s) over separator neighbors sx in E(C).
theorem.equivalence: C is list-colorable iff there exists psi in Col_L(S) such that every (Q_i,L_i^psi) is list-colorable.

proof.forward: Restrict any list-coloring of C to S and to each component; every component restriction respects the boundary-deleted lists.
proof.reverse: For one proper list-respecting psi on S, independently color every Q_i under L_i^psi and glue the colorings with psi; no edges join distinct Q_i.

theorem.reconstruction: Union all independently reconstructed component colorings with psi on S.
theorem.complexity_overhead: At most 4^3=64 raw separator assignments, plus polynomial component construction/list restriction and downstream terminal calls.

proof_carrying_certificate.component_partition: Verify components partition V(C)\S and no edge joins distinct components.
proof_carrying_certificate.per_psi: Verify psi is list-respecting/proper on C[S], propagate exact boundary restrictions, preserve downstream certificates.
proof_carrying_certificate.branch_logic: A psi branch is SAT iff every component is SAT; any exact contradiction/UNSAT component rejects the branch.
